From 05519b8589a679edb8fa781259893d20bece04ad Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Anssi Hannula <anssi.hannula@bitwise.fi>
Date: Thu, 3 Mar 2022 13:08:57 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] xhci: fix uninitialized string returned by
 xhci_decode_ctrl_ctx()

xhci_decode_ctrl_ctx() returns the untouched buffer as-is if both "drop"
and "add" parameters are zero.

Fix the function to return an empty string in that case.

It was not immediately clear from the possible call chains whether this
issue is currently actually triggerable or not.

Note that before commit 4843b4b5ec64 ("xhci: fix even more unsafe memory
usage in xhci tracing") the result effect in the failure case was different
as a static buffer was used here, but the code still worked incorrectly.

Fixes: 90d6d5731da7 ("xhci: Add tracing for input control context")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Anssi Hannula <anssi.hannula@bitwise.fi>
Signed-off-by: Mathias Nyman <mathias.nyman@linux.intel.com>

commit 4843b4b5ec64 ("xhci: fix even more unsafe memory usage in xhci tracing")
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220303110903.1662404-4-mathias.nyman@linux.intel.com

Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/host/xhci.h b/drivers/usb/host/xhci.h
index 1d83ddace482..473a33ce299e 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/host/xhci.h
+++ b/drivers/usb/host/xhci.h
@@ -2468,6 +2468,8 @@ static inline const char *xhci_decode_ctrl_ctx(char *str,
 	unsigned int	bit;
 	int		ret = 0;
 
+	str[0] = '\0';
+
 	if (drop) {
 		ret = sprintf(str, "Drop:");
 		for_each_set_bit(bit, &drop, 32)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/usb/host/xhci.h`**
   - A new line was added to initialize the string `str` to an empty string by setting the first character to the null terminator: `str[0] = '\0';`. This change ensures that if both the "drop" and "add" parameters are zero, the function `xhci_decode_ctrl_ctx()` will return an empty string instead of an uninitialized buffer.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `xhci.h` directly addresses a bug in the `xhci_decode_ctrl_ctx()` function. By initializing the string to an empty state, it prevents the function from returning an uninitialized string when both parameters are zero. This change is crucial for maintaining the integrity of the function's output and aligns with the intent to fix unsafe memory usage as noted in the commit message. The patch also references a previous commit that altered the behavior of the function, indicating that this fix is part of an ongoing effort to ensure safe and predictable memory handling in the xHCI driver.
